tagline.text: A white-sand beach on the Tañon Strait, on the way to Kawasan Falls

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Lambug, Badian, Cebu, on the southwest coast of Cebu

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (early mornings, when the sea is calm, are recommended)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day to one night

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (transport, entrance fee and snacks for a day trip from Cebu City, per person)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB), about 3–4 hours overland

children.text: Lambug Beach is a long white-sand beach in Barangay Lambug, Badian, on the southwest side of Cebu, and it pairs easily with a visit to nearby Kawasan Falls. Recent sources put the entrance fee at around ₱45 per person, and you can use cottages, camp or stay overnight, with the sun setting over the Tañon Strait toward Negros.
Lambug Beach is in Barangay Lambug in the municipality of Badian, on the southwest coast of Cebu island. It is about
3–4 hours

south of Cebu City, and many travelers combine it with the Kawasan Falls canyon outing in the same town of Badian. Two maps put it at roughly 9.853°N, 123.368°E. The beach faces west across the Tañon Strait toward Negros Island, so it is also known as a sunset spot. This guide is based on local news and travel blogs from recent years, so confirm prices and operating arrangements again before you go.

The beach is described as a long stretch of white sand with clear, relatively calm water. There are palm trees and shade, so it is not hard to find a place to rest even at midday, and cottages, lodging and small shops nearby make both day trips and overnight stays possible. Reviews in the same sources also mention rocky spots, days when seaweed washes ashore, and days when the water turns rough. Some visitors felt it looked better in photos than in person, so go expecting a simple local beach rather than resort-style facilities.

How the beach is run has changed several times. After Typhoon Odette struck southern Cebu at the end of 2021 it was closed for a while, and the municipality of Badian announced that it would reopen to the public on February 25, 2022. Under the guidelines then, food, drinks, picnics and tents were allowed in designated areas. A report says that in June 2023 the provincial government took over operations, stopped new construction and moved to enforce a 20-meter shoreline easement, but I could not confirm whether that arrangement still applies. The beach reportedly stayed open, so it is safest to check with the Badian Local Tourism office before you go.

Because it is close to the best-known waterfall canyon area in Badian, Lambug has become the beach people stop at when they have time left over on a Kawasan Falls day. Some people bring snorkeling gear, and many families play ball games such as volleyball. Some sources say you can see coral and marine life near the beach, but I could not confirm specific spots or visibility, so I will not claim more than that.

White sand runs along the shore for a long stretch. Several sources describe it as quiet, with tree shade that makes it good for resting. Some sections are rocky, so it is wise to wear footwear when you go into the water.
The beach faces west, so the sky turns red around sunset and the mountain ridges on the Negros side are visible across the water. If you stay into the evening on a clear day, it is very rewarding.

You can rent a cottage in the shade of the trees. According to 2021–2022 sources, a cottage for 10 people cost ₱1,000, one for 15 cost ₱1,800, and some were ₱500 a day, so negotiate and confirm according to group size and season.

A 2022 source says that pitching a tent you bring yourself costs ₱50 per person on weekdays and ₱150 per person on weekends. Tents may only be pitched in designated areas, so follow the on-site instructions.
Some sources say you can look underwater near the beach with a mask and snorkel. Visibility and currents vary by day, so start in shallow water and use safety gear.
A 2021 notice says volleyball equipment can be rented for ₱150 per hour. The sea is said to be calmer early in the day, so swimming in the morning is recommended.

Because it is close to Kawasan Falls in the same municipality of Badian, it is widely used as a place to rest after the canyon tour. The usual order is to see the falls in the morning and relax at the beach in the afternoon.
Reviews mention snack stalls at the corner of the beach road and small shops here and there along the beach. Dining choices are limited, so it is better to bring some food with you.

items.title: Day trip
items.subtitle: Leaving Cebu City in the morning

children.text: At the Cebu South Bus Terminal, board a bus bound for Bato via Barili. Allow
3–4 hours
for the ride, and tell the conductor in advance to drop you at the junction leading to Lambug Beach.
From the junction where you get off, take a tricycle or motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) to the beach. One source says it takes about
20–30 minutes
from the town center.
Pay the entrance fee and choose a cottage or a shady spot. The sea is said to be calmer in the morning, so swim and snorkel first.
Have lunch with the food you brought and rest. Shops on the beach may offer limited choices.
Relax in the shade and take photos as the sun gets lower. Be sure to check the time of the last bus back.
If you want to watch the sunset, stay until this time, but decide by comparing it with your return bus schedule.
Bus and tricycle times may change from year to year, so confirm them locally.

items.title: Two-day, one-night route
items.subtitle: Combining Kawasan Falls and the beach

children.text: Visit Kawasan Falls first and finish the canyon activities.
Move to Lambug, drop your bags at your lodging and relax on the beach. Watch the sunset in the evening.
Take an easy swim at dawn when the sea is calmest, then on the way back continue to Moalboal or other southern sights.
At the Cebu South Bus Terminal, take a bus bound for Bato via Barili. One source gives the ride as about
3–3.5 hours
, while another says 3.5–4 hours.

From Manila you must first fly to Cebu.
Fly from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB). Check airline notices for routes and times.
From the airport you can go to the Cebu South Bus Terminal and take the bus above, or go straight south by taxi or rental car.
Heading from Carcar Rotunda toward Barili, a sign for Lambug Beach reportedly stands on the right after you pass Badian town proper. One guide says it takes
20–25 minutes
from the junction to the beach.

From the Kawasan Falls area, one guide says a motorcycle taxi or tricycle costs around ₱50–100.

Southwest Cebu has stable weather from November to May, the dry season, which makes it the best time for a beach trip. In this period there are many days with calm waves and clear sunsets. In January and February the mornings and evenings are relatively cool and comfortable.

During the rainy season from June to October, showers and wind become frequent and the sea can turn rough. Reviews mention days when seaweed washes ashore, and facilities have stayed closed for a long time after a typhoon (Odette in 2021). In any month, many sources say early morning is calmest.

Around the beach you will find Lambug Beach Resort, smaller resorts and homestays. One source listed Angie's Beach House (₱1,700 a night, ₱1,500 off-peak), Lambug Beach Homestay (₱400 per person) and Grandeur Beach Resort (₱350 per person), but this is past information and may have changed. Many places accept groups in shared-room arrangements, and some allow you to cook food you bring yourself. Small shops sell simple drinks and snacks.

Restaurant choices are said to be limited. Some reviews advise bringing your own food, and some resorts have said they charge no corkage fee for outside food. There are also mentions of stalls at the beach road corner. Badian town proper has more varied places to eat, so shop there first if needed.
Fees for entrance and cottages change from year to year, so check in advance with an official contact such as the Badian Local Tourism office.
If you go on the same day as Kawasan Falls, the usual order is the falls first and the beach in the afternoon.
Bring food and water. Dining choices at the beach may be limited.
Some stretches are rocky, so aqua shoes are useful.
Many sources say the sea is calmer in the morning, so swim then.
Check the return bus times first and plan to reach the main road before dark.
Pitch tents only in designated areas and take your trash back with you.
Weekends and holidays draw crowds of groups, so go on a weekday if you can.
How the beach is run (entrance fee, facilities, construction limits) has changed several times, so check the latest notices.
Some stretches are rocky and seaweed washes ashore on some days, so be careful when entering the water.
Avoid swimming when the sea is rough, and do not go into deep water without a life jacket.
Guard against pickpocketing and loss by not leaving valuables unattended in the cottage.
Reviews mention that many people offer rooms, so politely decline if you do not need one.
The beach may close in typhoon season. Check notices before you leave.
